- When sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.1), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is negative (e.g., < -0.1); increase forecast by 0.5–2% to compensate.
- Mean reversion is strong in the 10–15 day horizon; if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent mean, adjust downward; if < 1.5σ below, adjust upward.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the 20–30 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for longer horizons.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
